Prototype first · Paper later

Two drones. No GPS. One shared sense of where they are.

Design and development of a UWB-Assisted Cooperative Two-UAV System for GPS-Denied Navigation — two identical quadcopters built from scratch that stabilise themselves, locate themselves indoors with Ultra-Wideband ranging + Visual-Inertial Odometry, talk to each other, hold formation, and are graded against a ~6-camera Motion Capture lab as independent ground truth.

2 × identicalquadcopters, independent FC + power each
~10 cmUWB ranging class (DS-TWR, IEEE 802.15.4z)
16.7 nslight-time for a 5 m range — why UWB timing is picosecond work
T/W ≥ 2.0design gate: hover near 50% throttle
9 phasesgated roadmap, Learn → Validate

01 · The pitch

Why this project matters — and why it's hard

GPS works outdoors. Warehouses, tunnels, factories, disaster sites and indoor labs are where GPS dies — and exactly where inspection, inventory and search drones are most needed. This project builds the navigation stack that replaces GPS, on real hardware, and proves it against MoCap ground truth.

🛰️ The problem

Indoors, GNSS signals are blocked or reflected into uselessness. An IMU alone drifts metres in under a minute. A camera alone fails in the dark, on blank walls, and has no scale. No single sensor solves indoor navigation.

📡 The idea

Fuse three imperfect senses: UWB gives absolute distance (no drift), VIO gives smooth direction & motion, the IMU gives high-rate attitude. Each covers the others' failure modes — and the two drones range to each other, not just to the room.

🤝 The cooperation

Two drones sharing ranges and odometry can localise better than either alone — and hold a formation with enforced safe separation. Flight-critical stabilisation stays local on each drone; Wi-Fi never sits in the fast loop.

02 · Live simulation

Watch it work: formation + UWB ranging, top-down

UAV-1 flies a circular path. UAV-2 follows at a fixed offset (leader–follower). The four corner anchors and the inter-drone link range continuously — watch the range readouts change. This is the exact geometry the real estimator will solve, 20 times a second.

Inter-drone range—
UAV-1 → Anchor A1—
UAV-2 → Anchor A1—
Separation statusSAFE
The one-range trap: the inter-drone link gives one number — a distance. Geometrically that's a sphere around UAV-1: UAV-2 could be anywhere on it. Direction only emerges from anchor ranges, VIO motion over time, or a camera bearing. Every design choice in this project follows from that single fact.

03 · Learn — Module A & B

The course: from zero to flight dynamics

Taught in the project's fixed pattern — What · Why · How · Theory · Equations · Components · Implement · Verify · What can go wrong · What success looks like. Open each lesson.

Lesson 1 — How a quadcopter flies & propulsion (start here)

Four propellers push air down; reaction pushes the drone up. Motors 1&3 spin one way, 2&4 the other, cancelling torque. Speed up a diagonal pair → yaw. Speed up the rear pair → pitch forward. Speed up the left pair → roll right. The flight controller does this mixing hundreds of times per second. We use X-configuration (forward between two motors): pitch and roll share all four motors and the camera gets a clear view.

Hover thrust per motor = All-Up Weight ÷ 4  ·  T/W = Total max thrust ÷ AUW (target ≥ 2.0)
T ∝ ρ · n² · D⁴ · CT  — diameter beats RPM  ·  RPM ≈ KV × Voltage

Worked example (illustrative, not the final design): AUW 1,800 g → 450 g hover thrust per motor → 900 g max per motor for T/W = 2. If a datasheet table gives ~6 A/motor at hover thrust: 24 A total, 4S 5,000 mAh ≈ 59 Wh usable → ≈ 10 min hover. A bigger battery adds weight → more thrust → more current: that loop is the design iteration.

Failure modes: CW/CCW props swapped, uncalibrated ESCs, prop vibration confusing the IMU, low C-rating voltage sag, off-centre CG. Success: you can explain T/W and why hover belongs near 50% throttle — without notes.

Lesson 2 — Flight mechanics: 6-DOF, frames, quaternions

Three translations (x, y, z) + three rotations (roll, pitch, yaw) = six degrees of freedom. The world frame (NED or ENU — pick one and never mix) is fixed to the room; the body frame is fixed to the drone. Rotation matrices convert between them; Euler angles gimbal-lock at ±90° pitch, so PX4 uses quaternions internally. Newton–Euler equations couple motor thrust to acceleration — the model PX4 SITL simulates before we ever spin a real prop.

Lesson 3 — Flight control: cascaded PID & state estimation

Control is nested loops: position loop (slow, ~10 Hz) asks for velocity → velocity loop asks for attitude → attitude/rate loop (fast, 250 Hz–1 kHz) drives motors. PID at each level: proportional reacts now, integral removes steady error, derivative damps overshoot. The estimator (EKF2 in PX4) fuses IMU + baro (+ VIO/UWB later) into one state. Rule for this project: this loop is local and flight-critical — no Wi-Fi, no ROS 2 in it.

05 · Crazy papers — read the giants

Papers & theses that prove this is real — MIT, IISc, IIT Hyderabad, TU Delft

Not blog posts. Peer-reviewed papers, arXiv preprints and institute theses — each one maps to a decision in our design. Tap any card to open the full text.

MIT · AEROSPACE CONTROLS LAB · IEEE RA-L 2024

MURP: Multi-Agent UWB Relative Pose Estimation in 3D

Fishberg, Quiter & How (MIT). Each drone carries six UWB antennas and gets full 3D relative pose from local ranges only — no continuous odometry streaming. Mean error: 0.24 m / 9.5°. 200+ hours of open datasets.

Steal this idea Multi-tag geometry breaks the one-range trap — our Phase-2 upgrade path.

MIT MEDIA LAB · IEEE INFOCOM 2025

MiFly: 6D Self-Localization with a Single mmWave Anchor

Lam, Dodds, Eid, Hester & Adib (MIT). One anchor, dark / occluded / GPS-denied, median 7 cm error. Proof that clever RF + IMU fusion can beat “add more cameras”.

Steal this idea Design the anchor and the algorithm together — don't bolt them together later.

TU DELFT · MAVLAB

Onboard Ranging-Based Relative Localization for Lightweight Aerial Swarms

Li, Shan & de Croon et al. First fully autonomous relative localisation on 13 drones of just 33 g (168 MHz MCU!), UWB + shared state, <0.2 m error at 16 Hz. Open-source code.

Steal this idea If 33 g drones can do it onboard, our Jetson-class build has no excuses.

IISc BENGALURU · AEROSPACE ENGINEERING

UAV Group Autonomy in Network-Centric Environments (IISc Thesis)

Full IISc thesis on cooperative UAV missions — including distributed cooperative localisation in GPS-denied environments, GPS-protected MAV networks mixing GPS / high-grade INS / low-grade INS, and layered persistent ISR replanning when UAVs fail.

Why it matters here Indian institute, same problem framing — formation + failure + GPS-denied, not just one drone hovering.

IISc BENGALURU · EVENT-CAMERA NAVIGATION

Navigation of Autonomous Vehicles using Event Cameras (IISc Thesis)

IISc work on real-time navigation in indoor, GPS-denied, unstructured spaces: event-camera Visual-Inertial Odometry (AeVIO), time-to-contact for collision avoidance, and kinematically-aware RRT planning extended to 3D UAV flight.

Watch this space Event cameras don't blur at speed — a future sensor option if our VIO breaks in fast manoeuvres.

IIT HYDERABAD · TiHAN — INDIA'S AUTONOMOUS NAV HUB

Deep RL Navigation of MAVs in GPS-Denied Indoor Environments — TiHAN Testbed

Singh, Duba & Rajalakshmi (IIT Hyderabad). Tested in the 30 × 30 × 8 m TiHAN testbed on a real DJI Tello, plus the TiHAN line on stereo-vision localisation for MAV autonomy in GPS-denied indoors. Browse all TiHAN publications →

Local benchmark TiHAN is the Indian facility model to compare our ~6-camera MoCap lab against.

How to read like an engineer (not a student cramming): For each paper — 1) What is measured? 2) What is ground truth? 3) What error, in metres / degrees, at what rate? 4) What breaks it (NLOS, darkness, speed)? MURP, Li et al. and MiFly all publish those four answers. If a paper hides them, downgrade it.

06 · Module C — UWB engineering

UWB deep-dive: measuring distance with light-speed timing

UWB sends very short radio pulses across a wide band (DWM3001C: channels 5 @ 6.5 GHz and 9 @ 8 GHz, IEEE 802.15.4z). Distance comes from time-of-flight — and light covers 30 cm in 1 ns, so the radio timestamps in picoseconds.

distance = c × ToF  ·  5.0 m → one-way ToF = 5.0 / 299,792,458 = 16.7 ns

SS-TWR vs DS-TWR — animated

Single-sided two-way ranging halves a round trip, but clock drift leaks straight into error. Double-sided TWR exchanges three messages and cancels most drift — that's what the drones will use. Press play and watch the exchange:

Poll → Response → Final · range solved from 3 timestamps each side

Key concepts

ToA / TDoA: arrival-time positioning (TDoA needs synchronised anchors). Trilateration: intersect range spheres from ≥4 anchors. AoA: angle from antenna arrays (not on DWM3001C — don't assume it). Multipath: reflections create late copies; first-path detection is the fight. NLOS: a body or wall blocking the direct path biases range long — detect and down-weight it.

Hardware under investigation

Qorvo DWM3001C — DW3110 transceiver + nRF52833 MCU + planar antenna + accelerometer, 27.1 × 19.13 mm, 2.5–3.6 V. DWM3001CDK — its dev kit for bench work. DWM3000 — bare module alternative. Indian price/availability: to be verified live from suppliers in Phase 3 — no price is quoted on this site until then.

Four UWB architectures — pick by stage, not by hype

Anchor geometry is accuracy. Four anchors in a line give terrible height estimates. Anchors must surround the volume with height variation and be surveyed precisely — we'll quantify it with dilution of precision (GDOP) before drilling a single mount.

07 · Module D — Visual-inertial navigation

VIO: the camera gives direction, the IMU gives speed of response

VIO tracks image features frame-to-frame, preintegrates IMU motion between frames, and solves for pose, velocity and biases in one estimator. It drifts slowly (~% of distance) but never jumps — the perfect partner for UWB's drift-free but noisy ranges.

AlgorithmTypeComputeVerdict for this project
OpenVINSFilter-based (MSCKF), tightly coupledLight — runs real-time on modest companion computersFirst choice. ROS 2 native; strong results on small platforms
VINS-FusionOptimisation-basedHeavierPhase-2 comparison; can struggle to initialise in rapid manoeuvres
ORB-SLAM3Full SLAM + loop closureHeaviestPhase-2 comparison; best long-term maps, most tuning
SVOSemi-direct VOLightReference only

Non-negotiables before VIO flies: camera calibration (intrinsics), camera–IMU extrinsic calibration, hardware time synchronisation, and vibration isolation — a blurry, time-shifted camera poisons the whole fusion.

08 · Modules G & H — System architecture

Three builds, one rule: calculations decide

Starting envelope to test (not a purchase decision): 450–500 mm class, under 2 kg (micro category in India). We pick A vs B only after the weight / thrust / battery sheet passes.

A · Minimum viable

Pixhawk 6C-class FC · Raspberry Pi 5-class companion · mono/stereo camera · 1× DWM3001C per drone · 4 anchors.

Lowest cost & weightPi may strain under VIO1 inter-drone range only

B · Recommended research-grade ★

Pixhawk 6C/6X-class FC · Jetson Orin Nano-class companion · stereo camera + IMU · 1× UWB per drone + 4–6 anchors, 2nd UWB node later.

Real-time OpenVINS headroomTests all UWB architecturesStill indoor-flyable

C · Advanced (Phase 2)

550–600 mm frame · Orin NX-class · stereo + LiDAR · 3× UWB per drone in a triangle (direct bearing) · 6–8 anchors.

Highest accuracy potentialHeaviest & hardest to tuneMay outgrow the MoCap volume

System block diagram — who talks to whom

Cooperative control choice: leader–follower formation control on top of a fused EKF state — feasible for two aircraft, debuggable, and safe: each drone enforces minimum separation locally even if the link drops. Consensus and MPC stay in the literature folder until the simple system is measured.

09 · Module I — Engineering calculations

Try the design loop yourself

Before any BOM exists, these calculations must pass. Drag the sliders — this is the exact iteration (weight → thrust → current → battery → weight) the team will run with real datasheet thrust tables.

Hover thrust / motor450 g
Thrust-to-weight2.04
Hover throttle (est.)~49%
Total hover current24 A
Hover power355 W
Endurance (80% usable)~10.0 min

Simplified model for learning: 4S nominal 14.8 V, endurance = usable Wh × 60 ÷ hover W. Real sign-off uses manufacturer thrust tables and measured current — estimated vs measured is always labelled in the project log.

Full calculation checklist (I1–I7)

  • I1 Weight budget — every gram, per drone
  • I2 Propulsion — hover/max thrust, KV, RPM, ESC rating
  • I3 Battery — S-count, C-rating, usable energy, endurance + 20% reserve
  • I4 Electrical — PDB, 5 V BEC budget, wire gauge, connectors
  • I5 Flight performance — hover time, climb, indoor speed limits
  • I6 Localisation — UWB σ, IMU/VIO drift, RMSE, latency budget
  • I7 Combined — ×2 drones + anchors + charging load

Pass gates

✔ T/W ≥ 2.0 at max thrust
✔ Hover throttle 45–60%
✔ Endurance computed with 20% battery reserve
✔ BEC 5 V budget covers companion + camera + UWB with margin
✔ Every number carries: equation, units, assumption, source

11 · Module E — Motion Capture lab

The referee: MoCap ground truth (~6 cameras — all specs UNVERIFIED)

MoCap is the independent judge of our estimator — never the thing being tested, and (in the main experiments) never fed into the flight controller. A separate optional experiment may later close the loop with MoCap, clearly labelled as such.

Facility checklist — take this to the lab in-charge

  • Manufacturer / model / software version?
  • Camera count — is it really 6? Tracking frequency (Hz)?
  • Tracking volume (L × W × H, metres)? Ceiling height?
  • Passive reflective or active markers? Rigid-body tracking?
  • Quoted position (mm) & orientation (°) accuracy?
  • Streaming: VRPN / NatNet / ROS / SDK? Which ROS package?
  • Frame convention: ENU/NED, origin, Z-up?
  • Latency camera → ROS topic? Synchronised rosbag recording?
  • Booking, safety (tether / net / prop guards), supervision rules?

Marker design (provisional)

4–5 markers per drone in an asymmetric pattern (symmetry makes orientation ambiguous), on stiff standoffs above props and camera, ≥10–15 cm apart, different pattern on UAV-1 vs UAV-2, never on arms that flex or on the removable battery. MoCap then yields: absolute position, orientation, relative separation, relative pose, formation error, and localisation drift — the exact numbers the final validation report will publish.

12 · Modules K & L — Roadmap & build stages

Nine phases. Every phase has a gate.

Indicative effort 20–28 weeks part-time depending on lab access and procurement — an estimate, re-planned after Phase 1. Nothing advances past a failed gate.

Phase 0 — Learn

Modules A–B. Gate: explain thrust, PID, and why one UWB range isn't a position.

Phase 1 — Define + Calculate

Requirements, design envelope, Module I sheet. Gate: weight/thrust/battery signed off by mentor.

Phase 2 — Software + Simulation

Stack install → 1-drone SITL → 2-drone SITL → GPS-denied SITL. Gate: two simulated drones hold position with no GPS.

Phase 3 — BOM + Procurement

Three budget scenarios, live Indian supplier checks, DGCA/WPC check. Gate: BOM approved — nothing ordered on an invented price.

Phase 4 — Build UAV-1

Assembly, calibration, tethered hover, manual flight. Gate: stable manual hover + failsafe land.

Phase 5 — Build UAV-2

Duplicate exactly, verify identical. Gate: both fly independently.

Phase 6 — UWB + VIO

Bench ranging → anchor survey → OpenVINS bench → flight. Gate: UWB RMSE & VIO drift measured vs MoCap.

Phase 7 — Cooperative flight

Inter-drone link, relative estimator, leader–follower. Gate: formation held in the MoCap volume, safe separation enforced locally.

Phase 8 — Validate + Document

MoCap validation runs, error tables, this site updated as the engineering notebook. Gate: results are measured, not claimed.

Regulatory checkpoints (verify with mentor before flight/transmission): India classes — nano ≤250 g, micro 250 g–2 kg (UIN required for micro and above); complete drones in CBU/SKD/CKD form have been import-prohibited since Feb 2022 (another reason this is a build-from-parts project); UWB radio operation needs a WPC check in Phase 3.

13 · Module J — BOM status

The BOM does not exist yet — on purpose

A shopping list written before the calculations is how projects burn money. The BOM is a Phase-3 deliverable, built from the passed Module I sheet, with three scenarios (minimum viable / recommended research-grade / advanced), separate lists for UAV-1, UAV-2, shared infrastructure, ground station and safety gear — every line with datasheet, live INR price and Indian supplier link, verified at purchase time. Nothing on this page invents a price.

Per drone (×2, identical)

Frame · 4× motors · 4× ESCs (or 4-in-1) · props + spares · FC · companion · camera · UWB · battery · PDB · BEC · RC receiver · telemetry · wiring · vibration mounts · marker mounts

Shared infrastructure

4–8 UWB anchors + mounts + power · DWM3001CDK bench kits · ground-station laptop · RC transmitter · charger + fire-safe bag · spare batteries/props/fasteners

Safety & test

Prop guards · tether/net per lab rules · RC kill switch · multimeter · thrust stand (if lab has one — don't buy yet) · flight log book · eye protection

14 · Decisions needed

10 questions that lock the design

Answer in short lines — blanks are fine. Nothing gets guessed: these answers feed Phase 1 requirements directly.

  1. Team members + mentor / lab in-charge for sign-off?
  2. MoCap system identity — checklist answers, or a photo of the cameras + software screen?
  3. Indoor flight volume, ceiling height, lab safety rules?
  4. Budget ceiling or per-drone target range?
  5. PC/GPU specs available for ROS 2 + Gazebo + VIO?
  1. Target flight time & payload (e.g. ~10 min, camera + UWB only)?
  2. Is 450–500 mm acceptable for the MoCap volume & transport?
  3. Existing shared gear (transmitter, charger, 3D printer)? Old drone hardware is not reused — ground gear is different.
  4. Indoor only, or outdoor GPS-denied (e.g. warehouse) later?
  5. Demo / submission deadline, if any?
